verdict.rationale: Sill mainly streams one Mac window or the whole desktop to an iPhone or iPad, which is mirroring. Its optional virtual display does move a streamed window onto a separate display of its own on the Mac, so the device shows content that is not on the main screen. That is a narrow, single-window form of extension, and the docs frame it as a way to keep the window updating when covered, not as a second monitor. missing for 10: a documented extended-desktop mode where the device acts as an additional monitor, dragging windows freely between the Mac screen and the device, display arrangement or resolution settings, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, a tablet or spare device works as an additional display that extends the desktop, not only a mirror of it

citations.quote: The virtual display (off by default) moves a window you stream onto a display of its own on your Mac, so it keeps updating when other windows cover it.
Sill shows a window from your Mac, or its whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad
